text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 0.7% today to $427.34, extending a 10% decline over two weeks despite strong refining conditions. The stock got hit on the heels of the company's quarterly earnings report and a leadership change announced today; broader sector caution also weighed on it, as analysts flagged that Big Oil earnings guidance—what companies say they'll earn going forward—matters more than the headline numbers themselves, and price charts suggested a pullback was coming.

The refining backdrop remains solid: U.S. crude is holding near $103 per barrel, refineries are running at 92.8% capacity (well above typical levels), and storage levels for gasoline and diesel are moderate. But the market appears focused on what guidance means for profitability ahead, especially given political uncertainty around energy policy following the midterms. That makes near-term sentiment fragile, even when operational conditions stay favorable.
